title: The Evening Brief: Senate kills Clarity Act; Circle launches Arc with Wall Street validators
dek: The Senate blocked the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act on a 49-50 cloture vote Tuesday, ending a year of bipartisan negotiations over ethics provisions. Meanwhile, Circle's Arc blockchain launches Wednesday with BlackRock, DTCC, Visa, and Mastercard as founding validators, a structural bet that institutional settlement will draw institutional guardrails.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: The Clarity Act's failure signals that crypto regulation will not move through Congress this year, leaving the SEC and CFTC to define oversight unilaterally. Arc's launch embeds major financial institutions into consensus finality while explicitly disclaiming validator liability for applications, a model that tests whether Wall Street will operate settlement infrastructure without assuming custody risk.
bottom_line: The Senate's Clarity Act failure leaves crypto regulation in the hands of the SEC and CFTC through rulemaking timelines measured in months. Circle's Arc launch Wednesday embeds Wall Street validators into settlement finality while explicitly walling off their liability for applications, the first live test of whether institutions will operate infrastructure without custody risk. Monitor whether Arc accumulates institutional settlement volume before the May 2028 ARC token delivery deadline, and track the SEC's October 2026 custody-rule notice target and the House Ways and Means Committee markup on September 16 to see whether tax or custody clarity can move legislatively if the Clarity Act remains blocked.
body: The Senate voted 49-50 on Tuesday to block the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633), the first comprehensive federal crypto framework. A cloture motion needed 60 votes to proceed to floor debate. Four Senate Republicans, Susan Collins, Josh Hawley, Jerry Moran, and Thom Tillis, joined all Democrats in voting no. The deadlock centered on ethics provisions governing whether sitting officials, including President Trump, could hold financial interests in crypto ventures while their administrations regulated the industry. Seven Democratic negotiators who had spent a year shaping the bill, Mark Warner, Angela Alsobrooks, Cory Booker, Catherine Cortez Masto, Ruben Gallego, Raphael Warnock, and Kirsten Gillibrand, said the final Republican language was insufficient to prevent conflicts of interest. The House passed the bill 294-134 in July 2025. Unless Senator Tillis forces a second cloture vote before the state work period closes October 5, the Clarity Act remains dead this Congress, per the reporting.

The bill's failure leaves crypto oversight to the SEC and CFTC through rulemaking. The SEC's custody rule rewrite (RIN 3235-AN46) entered White House OMB review on August 25 and targets October 2026 for a notice of proposed rulemaking, though that date is an internal target with no binding deadline. The House Ways and Means Committee released a 114-page Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act on September 14 with a formal markup set for September 16, but the bill faces survival pressure from compressed legislative calendars before November elections.

Circle's Arc mainnet launches September 16 with 11 named founding validators: BlackRock, DTCC, Visa, Mastercard, ICE, and six additional institutions. The validators operate a permissioned Proof-of-Authority consensus; a rotating validator proposes a block, and more than two-thirds of the validator set must pre-commit before the block is finalized and cannot be reorganized at the consensus layer. Circle has stated the launch configuration will include about 20 SOC 2-certified validators across multiple regions, more than the 12 public names. Crucially, Circle's documentation explicitly disclaims that Arc Network Services LLC or any validator bears responsibility for third-party applications or their content, meaning the institutions securing the network assume no custody or liability risk for what developers build on top of Arc. BlackRock was an investor in Circle's ARC token presale and plans to deploy its BUIDL money-market fund on Arc; DTCC is both a founding validator and an integration partner, with DTC-custodied assets targeted for the second half of 2027. Circle's presale agreements require ARC tokens to be delivered or Arc to transition to Proof-of-Stake by May 2028, or presale purchasers holding a majority of the allocation may demand repayment.

The desk's ETF flows board shows Bitcoin outflows of $288.7 million on September 15 and net outflows of $544.9 million over the past five sessions, an extended period of withdrawal despite the monthly gain. Ethereum closed at $2,399.09, flat on the day but down 4.57 percent over the week and up 28.39 percent over 30 days; ETH saw an outflow of $56.7 million on the day but a net inflow of $285.6 million over five sessions, meaning the direction reversed this week. The desk's whale flows board shows $76,868,173 in bitcoin moving onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, with Binance as the destination, and $28,657,500 in Cronos (CRO) moving off Crypto.com. The Fear and Greed Index registered 51 (Neutral), within a 30-day range of 41 to 74. Bitcoin's RSI14 stood at 49.1 and Ethereum's at 50.4, both indicating neither overbought nor oversold conditions. MACD remained below the signal line across major assets. Derivatives showed Bitcoin open interest at $2.12 billion with a long-short ratio of 1.78 and 6.5 percent annualized funding on OKX. Ethereum's open interest reached $1.51 billion with a 2.11 long-short ratio and 3.4 percent annualized funding, both showing elevated long positioning and sustained funding costs.

Institutional infrastructure moves continued. S&P Global led a Series B extension of Kaiko, a crypto data provider, to $110 million, more than double the $53 million original 2022 round. BNP Paribas, Broadridge, Nasdaq Ventures, Royal Bank of Canada, and nine other financial and venture firms participated. India's tokenized corporate bond pilot, Demat 2.0, completed three issuances totaling ₹1,025 crore using atomic delivery-versus-payment between private digital bonds and the wholesale central bank rupee, with retail access and secondary trading deferred to a later stage. Revolut began rolling out EURR, a euro-backed stablecoin issued by Bridge Building S.A., a Luxembourg-authorized electronic money institution, with Bridge holding €374 in circulation as of late August.

Security and governance pressures mounted. The DOJ filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking $61 million in cryptocurrency allegedly held in Binance accounts controlled by two China-based entities used to launder Iranian oil proceeds destined for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, as part of Operation Economic Outcast. The DOJ separately charged two Robinhood engineers, Hefu Chai and Huaisong Xiang, with wire fraud and commodities fraud for allegedly trading perpetual futures on Hyperliquid using nonpublic information about cryptocurrency listings. Balancer's governance forum posted a shutdown proposal on September 14 after monthly protocol revenue fell to $30,000 against $150,000 monthly burn, breaching the $60,000 revenue floor set in April's restructuring vote. The Snapshot vote is scheduled for September 25-29, with the first redemption window opening May 31, 2027 if approved. Symbiosis recovered 15 BTC and offered a 20 percent bounty after a bridge exploit created 46.1 billion syBTC from a 330-satoshi deposit; the protocol estimates preliminary losses at 9.97 BTC, approximately $770,000. CoinEx, a Hong Kong exchange, announced it will cease operations in December after nine years, citing falling volumes, compliance costs, and security risks.
